prompt: The PDA for aⁿbⁿ starts with `$` on its stack, pushes `A` for each `a`, pops an `A` for each `b`, and accepts only if it reaches `$` with all input read. What happens on input `aab`?

options.text: Accepts, because every b matched an A
options.explanation: Every b did match, but one A is left over. The machine can only reach the accepting state when `$` is back on top.

options.text: Rejects, because after the input ends the stack is `A$`, so the bottom-marker pop move to the accepting state is not available
options.explanation: Correct. Two pushes and one pop leave one A above `$`. No branch can reach f with the input consumed.

options.text: Rejects, because the PDA crashes when it reads the first b
options.explanation: Reading b with A on top is exactly the allowed pop move. Nothing goes wrong until the end.

Every branch of this particular PDA makes only a bounded number of epsilon state changes, and its other moves consume input. In general, the absence of epsilon pushes alone does not rule out epsilon cycles.

workedExample:
Trace it (stack top on the left):

```
read a  push A   stack A$
read a  push A   stack AA$
jump p→q (ε)
read b  pop A    stack A$
end of input
```

To accept, the PDA needs `$` on top so it can pop the bottom marker and enter the accepting state without consuming input. The top is A, so no move applies. Every other branch (jumping to q earlier, for instance) gets stuck sooner. Reject.

prompt: A bracket checker must remember arbitrarily many pending opening brackets and close the most recent one first. Which extra memory gives a finite automaton the PDA model suited to this nesting?

options.text: A random-access array of unbounded size
options.explanation: That would be more like a random-access machine or Turing machine. A PDA's extra memory can only be read at one end.

options.text: An unbounded stack that it can read and change only at the top
options.explanation: Correct. The stack gives unbounded memory but with last-in, first-out access, exactly what matching nested brackets needs.

options.text: A second input tape that it can rewind
options.explanation: PDAs read their single input once, left to right. Rewinding input is not part of the model.

options.text: Nothing; it is the same machine with a different name
options.explanation: A PDA is strictly more powerful: it recognises aⁿbⁿ, which no NFA can.

workedExample:
1. An NFA's only memory is which state it is in: finitely many possibilities.
2. A PDA adds a stack. Each move may pop the top symbol and push new ones.
3. Access is restricted to the top, so it cannot access arbitrary stored cells as a TM can. The fact that aⁿbⁿcⁿ is impossible is established by the CFL pumping proof, not merely this informal memory analogy.
